~14 So the LORD {YHWH} sent a plague upon Israel (he wrestles with God), and seventy thousand men of Israel fell dead.
~15 Then God {Elohim} sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem (city of peace), but as the angel was doing so, the LORD {YHWH} saw it and relented from the calamity, and He said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan (Araunah) the Jebusite (Jerusalemite).
~16 When David (beloved) lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD {YHWH} standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem (city of peace), David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown.
~17 And David (beloved) said to God {Elohim}, “Was it not I who gave the order to count the people? I (I, the shepherd,) am the one who has sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? O LORD my God {YHWH Elohay}, please let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house, but do not let this plague remain upon Your people.”
~18 Then the angel of the LORD {YHWH} ordered Gad (troop) to tell David (beloved) to go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan (light was perpetuated) the Jebusite (Jerusalemite).
~19 So David (beloved) went up at the word that Gad (troop) had spoken in the name of the LORD {YHWH}.
~20 Now Ornan (light was perpetuated) was threshing wheat when he turned and saw the angel; and his four sons who were with him hid themselves.
~21 David (beloved) came to Ornan (light was perpetuated), and when Ornan looked out and saw David, he left the threshing floor and bowed facedown before David.
~22 Then David (beloved) said to Ornan (light was perpetuated), “Grant me the site of this threshing floor, that I may build an altar to the LORD {YHWH}. Sell it to me for the full price, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”
~23 Ornan (light was perpetuated) said to David (beloved), “Take it! May my lord the king do whatever seems good to him. Look, I will give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood, and the wheat for the grain offering—I will give it all.”
~24 “No,” replied (light was perpetuated) King David (beloved), “I insist on paying the full price, for I will not take for the LORD {YHWH} what belongs to you, nor will I offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing.”
~25 So David (beloved) paid Ornan (light was perpetuated) six hundred shekels of gold <15.1 lb / 6.8 kg> for the site.
~26 And (beloved) there he built an altar to the LORD {YHWH} and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called upon the LORD, who answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.
~27 Then the LORD {YHWH} spoke to the angel, who put his sword back into its sheath.
~28 At that time, when David (beloved) saw that the LORD {YHWH} had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan (light was perpetuated) the Jebusite (Jerusalemite), he offered sacrifices there.
~29 For the tabernacle of the LORD {YHWH} that Moses (drawn out) had made in the wilderness and the altar of burnt offering were presently at the high place in Gibeon (hill city),
~30 but David (beloved) could not go before it to inquire of God {Elohim}, because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD {YHWH}.
chapters.1 Chronicles\u000022:
~1 Then David (beloved) said, “Here shall be the house of the LORD God {YHWH Elohim}, as well as the altar of burnt offering for Israel (he wrestles with God).”
~2 So David (beloved) gave orders to gather the foreigners in the land of Israel (he wrestles with God), from whom he appointed stonecutters to prepare finished stones for building the house of God {Elohim}.
~3 David (beloved) provided a large quantity of iron to make the nails for the doors of the gateways and for the fittings, together with more bronze than could be weighed
~4 and more cedar logs than could be counted; for the Sidonians and Tyrians had brought a large quantity of cedar logs to David (beloved).
~5 And David (beloved) said, “My son Solomon (peace) is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD {YHWH} must be exceedingly magnificent—famous and glorious throughout all lands. Therefore I must make preparations for it.” So David made lavish preparations before his death.
~6 Then David called for his son Solomon (peace) and instructed him to build a house for the LORD, the God {YHWH Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God).
~7 “My son,” said David (beloved) to Solomon (peace), “it was in my heart to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God {YHWH Elohay},
~8 but this word of the LORD {YHWH} came to me: ‘You have shed much blood and waged great wars. You are not to build a house for My Name because you have shed so much blood on the ground before Me.
~9 But a son will be born to you who will be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side; for his name will be Solomon (peace), and I will grant to Israel (he wrestles with God) peace and quiet during his reign.
~10 He is the one who will build a house for My Name. He will be My son, and I will be his Father. And I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel (he wrestles with God) forever.’
~11 Now, my son, may the LORD {YHWH} be with you, and may you succeed in building the house of the LORD your God {YHWH Eloheka}, as He said you would.
~12 Above all, may the LORD {YHWH} give you insight and understanding when He puts you in command over Israel (he wrestles with God), so that you may keep the Law of the LORD your God {YHWH Eloheka}.
~13 Then you will succeed, if you carefully follow the statutes and ordinances that the LORD {YHWH} commanded Moses (drawn out) for Israel (he wrestles with God). Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged.
~14 Now behold, I have taken great pains to provide for the house of the LORD {YHWH}—100,000 talents of gold <3,770 t / 3,420 mt>, 1,000,000 talents of silver <37,700 t / 34,200 mt>, and bronze and iron too great to be weighed. I have also provided timber and stone, and you may add to them.
~15 You also have many workers: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and men skilled in every kind of work—
~16 in gold and silver, bronze and iron—craftsmen beyond number. Now begin the work, and may the LORD {YHWH} be with you.”
~17 Then David (beloved) ordered all the leaders of Israel (he wrestles with God) to help his son Solomon (peace):
~18 “Is not the LORD your⁺ God {YHWH Eloheikem} with you⁺, and has He not granted you⁺ rest on every side? For He has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has been subdued before the LORD and His people.
~19 Now set your⁺ heart and soul to seek the LORD your⁺ God {YHWH Eloheikem}. Begin building the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you⁺ may bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy articles of God into the temple that will be built for the Name of the LORD.”
chapters.1 Chronicles\u000023:
~1 When David (beloved) was old and full of years, he installed his son Solomon (peace) as king over Israel (he wrestles with God).
~2 Then he gathered all the leaders of Israel (he wrestles with God), as well as the priests and Levites.
~3 The Levites thirty years of age or older were counted, and the total number of men was 38,000.
~4 “Of these,” said David, “24,000 are to oversee the work of the house of the LORD {YHWH}, 6,000 are to be officers and judges,
~5 4,000 are to be gatekeepers, and 4,000 are to praise the LORD {YHWH} with the instruments I have made for giving praise.”
~6 Then David (beloved) divided the Levites into divisions according to the sons of Levi (joined to): Gershon (exile), Kohath (assembly), and Merari (bitter).
~7 The Gershonites: Ladan (Libni) and Shimei (renowned).
~8 The sons of Ladan (put in order): Jehiel (Jehieli) the first, Zetham (olive), and Joel (YHWH is God)—three in all.
~9 The sons of Shimei (renowned): Shelomoth (peaceful), Haziel (vision of God), and Haran (mountaineer)—three in all. These were the heads of the families of Ladan (put in order).
~10 And the sons of Shimei (Shimei): Jahath (He will snatch up), Zina [Zizah], Jeush (He hurries to aid), and Beriah (with a friend). These were the sons of Shimei (renowned)—four in all.
~11 Jahath (He will snatch up) was the first and Zizah (abundance) was the second; but Jeush (He hurries to aid) and Beriah (with a friend) did not have many sons, so they were counted as one family and received a single assignment.
~12 The sons of Kohath (assembly): Amram (exalted people), Izhar (shining oil), Hebron (association), and Uzziel (my strength is God)—four in all.
~13 The sons of Amram (exalted people): Aaron (light bringer) and Moses (drawn out). Aaron and his descendants were set apart forever to consecrate the most holy things, to burn incense before the LORD {YHWH}, to minister before Him, and to pronounce blessings in His name forever.
~14 As for Moses (drawn out) the man of God {Elohim}, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi (joined to).
~15 The sons of Moses (drawn out): Gershom (foreigner) and Eliezer (God is my helper).
~16 The descendants of Gershom (foreigner): Shebuel (captive of God) was the first.
~17 The descendants of Eliezer (God is my helper): Rehabiah (YHWH has enlarged) was the first. Eliezer did not have any other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very numerous.
~18 The sons of Izhar (shining oil): Shelomith (peaceful) was the first.
~19 The sons of Hebron (association): Jeriah (taught by Yah) was the first, Amariah (YHWH has promised) the second, Jahaziel (beheld of God) the third, and Jekameam (let the people rise) the fourth.
~20 The sons of Uzziel (my strength is God): Micah (who is like God) was the first and Isshiah (YHWH will lend) the second.
~21 The sons of Merari (bitter): Mahli (sick) and Mushi (yielding). The sons of Mahli: Eleazar (God has helped) and Kish (bent).
~22 Eleazar (God has helped) died without having any sons; he had only daughters. Their cousins, the sons of Kish (bent), married them.
~23 The sons of Mushi (yielding): Mahli (sick), Eder (a flock), and Jeremoth (Jerimoth) three in all.
~24 These were the descendants of Levi (joined to) by their families—the heads of families, registered individually by name—those twenty years of age or older who worked in the service of the house of the LORD {YHWH}.
~25 For David (beloved) had said, “The LORD, the God {YHWH Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God), has given rest to His people and has come to dwell in Jerusalem (city of peace) forever.
~26 So now the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service.”
~27 For according to the final instructions of David (beloved), the Levites (joined to) twenty years of age or older were counted,
~28 but their duty was to assist the descendants of Aaron (light bringer) with the service of the house of the LORD {YHWH}, being responsible for the courts and chambers, the purification of all the holy things, and the work of the service of the house of God {Elohim},
~29 as well as for the rows of the showbread, the fine flour for the grain offering, the wafers of unleavened bread, the baking, the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size.
~30 They were also to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD {YHWH}, and likewise in the evening.
~31 Whenever burnt offerings were presented to the LORD {YHWH} on the Sabbaths, New Moons, and appointed feasts, they were to serve regularly before the LORD in the numbers prescribed for them.
~32 So the Levites were to carry out the responsibilities for the Tent of Meeting and the Holy Place, and, under their brothers the descendants of Aaron (light bringer), the service of the house of the LORD {YHWH}.
chapters.1 Chronicles\u000024:
~1 These were the divisions of the descendants of Aaron (light bringer). The sons of Aaron were Nadab (generous), Abihu (he is my father), Eleazar (God has helped), and Ithamar (coast of palms).
~2 But Nadab (generous) and Abihu (he is my father) died before their father did, and they had no sons; so Eleazar (God has helped) and Ithamar (coast of palms) served as priests.
~3 With the help of Eleazar’s (God has helped) descendant Zadok (righteous) and Ithamar’s (coast of palms) descendant Ahimelech (my brother is king), David (beloved) divided them according to the offices of their service.
~4 Since more leaders were found among Eleazar’s (God has helped) descendants than those of Ithamar (coast of palms), they were divided accordingly. There were sixteen heads of families from the descendants of Eleazar and eight from the descendants of Ithamar.
~5 Thus they were divided by lot, for there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God {Elohim} among both Eleazar’s (God has helped) and Ithamar’s (coast of palms) descendants.
~6 The scribe, Shemaiah (heard by YHWH) son of Nethanel (given of God), a Levite, recorded their names in the presence of the king and of the officers: Zadok (righteous) the priest, Ahimelech (my brother is king) son of Abiathar (my father is great), and the heads of families of the priests and the Levites—one family being taken from Eleazar (God has helped), and then one from Ithamar (coast of palms).
~7 The first lot fell to Jehoiarib (YHWH contends), the second to Jedaiah (YHWH has known),
~8 the third to Harim (dedicated), the fourth to Seorim (barley),
~9 the fifth to Malchijah (my king is YHWH), the sixth to Mijamin (from the right hand),
~10 the seventh to Hakkoz (thorn), the eighth to Abijah (YHWH is my father),
~11 the ninth to Jeshua (he is saved), the tenth to Shecaniah (dweller with YHWH),
~12 the eleventh to Eliashib (God restores), the twelfth to Jakim (He will raise),
~13 the thirteenth to Huppah (canopy), the fourteenth to Jeshebeab (dwelling of the father),
~14 the fifteenth to Bilgah (cheerfulness), the sixteenth to Immer (he has said),
~15 the seventeenth to Hezir (swine), the eighteenth to Happizzez (to break),
~16 the nineteenth to Pethahiah (freed by YHWH), the twentieth to Jehezkel (God strengthens),
~17 the twenty-first to Jachin (He will establish), the twenty-second to Gamul (weaned),
~18 the twenty-third to Delaiah (YHWH has drawn), and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah (consolation of YHWH).
~19 This was their appointed order for service when they entered the house of the LORD {YHWH}, according to the regulations prescribed for them by their forefather Aaron (light bringer), as the LORD, the God {Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God), had commanded him.
~20 Now these were the rest of the descendants of Levi (joined to): From the sons of Amram (exalted people): Shubael (Shebuel); from the sons of Shubael (captive of God): Jehdeiah (YHWH is unity).
~21 As for Rehabiah (YHWH has enlarged), from his sons: The first was Isshiah (Jeshaiah).
~22 From the Izharites (oil): Shelomoth (Shelomith); from the sons of Shelomoth (peaceful): Jahath (He will snatch up).
~23 From the sons of Hebron: Jeriah was the first \From the sons: Jeriah/, Amariah (YHWH has promised) the second, Jahaziel (beheld of God) the third, and Jekameam (let the people rise) the fourth.
~24 From the sons of Uzziel (my strength is God): Micah (who is like God); from the sons of Micah: Shamir (guardian).
~25 The brother of Micah (who is like God): Isshiah (YHWH will lend); from the sons of Isshiah: Zechariah (YHWH remembers).
~26 The sons of Merari (bitter): Mahli (sick) and Mushi (yielding). The son of Jaaziah (made bold by YHWH): Beno.
~27 The descendants of Merari (bitter) from Jaaziah (made bold by YHWH): Beno, Shoham (onyx), Zaccur (mindful), and Ibri (Hebrew).
~28 From Mahli (sick): Eleazar (God has helped), who had no sons.
~29 From Kish (bent): Jerahmeel (may God have pity) the son of Kish.
~30 And the sons of Mushi (yielding): Mahli (sick), Eder (a flock), and Jerimoth (Jeremoth). These were the sons of the Levites, according to their families.
~31 As their brothers the descendants of Aaron did (light bringer), they also cast lots in the presence of King David (beloved) and of Zadok (righteous), Ahimelech (my brother is king), and the heads of the families of the priests and Levites—the family heads and their younger brothers alike.
chapters.1 Chronicles\u000026:
~1 These were the divisions of the gatekeepers: From the Korahites (one of Korah): Meshelemiah (whom YHWH repays) son of Kore (crier), one of the sons of Asaph (gatherer).
~2 Meshelemiah (whom YHWH repays) had sons: Zechariah (YHWH remembers) the firstborn, Jediael (God makes known) the second, Zebadiah (endowment of YHWH) the third, Jathniel (God hires me) the fourth,
~3 Elam (eternity) the fifth, Jehohanan (YHWH has graced) the sixth, and Eliehoenai (unto YHWH are my eyes) the seventh.
~4 And Obed-edom (servant of Edom) also had sons: Shemaiah (heard by YHWH) the firstborn, Jehozabad (YHWH has endowed) the second, Joah (YHWH is brother) the third, Sachar (wages) the fourth, Nethanel (given of God) the fifth,
~5 Ammiel (my kinsman is God) the sixth, Issachar (there is recompense) the seventh, and Peullethai (work) the eighth. For God {Elohim} had blessed Obed-edom.
~6 Also to his son Shemaiah (heard by YHWH) were born sons who ruled over their families because they were strong, capable men.
~7 Shemaiah’s (heard by YHWH) sons were Othni (lion of YHWH), Rephael (healed of God), Obed (serving), and Elzabad (God has given); his brothers were Elihu (He is my God) and Semachiah (YHWH has sustained), also capable men.
~8 All these were descendants of Obed-edom (servant of Edom); they and their sons and brothers were capable men with strength to do the work—62 in all from Obed-edom.
~9 Meshelemiah (whom YHWH repays) also had sons and brothers who were capable men—18 in all.
~10 Hosah (refuge) the Merarite (bitter) also had sons: Shimri (vigilant) the first (although he was not the firstborn, his father had appointed him as the first),
~11 Hilkiah (my portion is YHWH) the second, Tebaliah (purified) the third, and Zechariah (YHWH remembers) the fourth. The sons and brothers of Hosah (refuge) numbered 13 in all.
~12 These divisions of the gatekeepers, through their chief men, had duties for ministering in the house of the LORD {YHWH}, just as their relatives did.
~13 They cast lots for each gate, according to their families, young and old alike.
~14 The lot for the East Gate fell to Shelemiah (Meshelemiah). Then lots were cast for his son Zechariah (YHWH remembers), a wise counselor, and the lot for the North Gate fell to him.
~15 The lot for the South Gate fell to Obed-edom (servant of Edom), and the lot for the storehouses to his sons.
~16 The lots for the West Gate and the Shallecheth (overthrow) Gate on the ascending highway (on the upper road) fell to Shuppim (serpents) and Hosah (refuge). There were guards stationed at every watch.
~17 Each day there were six Levites on the east, four on the north, four on the south, and two pairs at the storehouse.
~18 As for the court {parbar} on the west, there were four at the highway and two at the court (open apartment).
~19 These were the divisions of the gatekeepers who were descendants of Korah (one of Korah) and Merari (bitter).
~20 Now their fellow Levites were [As for the Levites, Ahijah was] in charge of the treasuries of the house of God {Elohim} and the treasuries of the dedicated things.
~21 From the descendants of Ladan (put in order), who were Gershonites through Ladan (Libni) and heads of the families of Ladan the Gershonite, were Jehieli (Jehiel),
~22 the sons of Jehieli (God shall save alive), Zetham (olive), and his brother Joel (YHWH is God). They were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD {YHWH}.
~23 From the Amramites, the Izharites (oil), the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
~24 Shebuel (captive of God), a descendant of Gershom (foreigner) son of Moses (drawn out), was the officer in charge of the treasuries.
~25 His relatives through Eliezer included (God is my helper) Rehabiah (YHWH has enlarged) his son, Jeshaiah (Isshiah) his son, Joram (YHWH is exalted) his son, Zichri (memorable) his son, and Shelomith (peaceful) his son.
~26 This Shelomith (peaceful) and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries for the things dedicated by King David (beloved), by the heads of families who were the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and by the army commanders.
~27 They had dedicated some of the plunder from their battles to the repair of the house of the LORD {YHWH}.
~28 Everything that had been dedicated by Samuel (his name is El) the seer, Saul (desired) son of Kish (bent), Abner (my father is a lamp) son of Ner (lamp), and Joab (YHWH is father) son of Zeruiah (balsam), along with everything else that was dedicated, was under the care of Shelomith (peaceful) and his brothers.
~29 From the Izharites (oil), Chenaniah (YHWH establishes) and his sons had the outside duties (the duties outside the temple) as officers and judges over Israel (he wrestles with God).
~30 From the Hebronites, Hashabiah (YHWH has considered) and his relatives, 1,700 capable men, had charge of the affairs of Israel (he wrestles with God) west of the Jordan (flowing down) for all the work of the LORD {YHWH} and for the service of the king.
~31 As for the Hebronites, Jerijah (Jeriah) was the chief of the Hebronites, according to the genealogies of his ancestors. In the fortieth year of David’s (beloved) reign the records were searched, and strong, capable men were found among the Hebronites at Jazer (helped) in Gilead (rocky region).
~32 Among Jerijah’s relatives there were 2,700 capable men who were heads of families. King David (beloved) appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites (a troop / fortune), and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter pertaining to God {Elohim} and for the affairs of the king.
chapters.1 Chronicles\u000027:
~1 This is the list of the Israelites (God prevails)—the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in every matter concerning the divisions on rotating military duty each month throughout the year. There were 24,000 men in each division:
~2 Jashobeam (the people will return) son of Zabdiel (God is my endowment) was in charge of the first division, which was assigned the first month. There were 24,000 men in his division.
~3 He was a descendant of Perez (breaking out) and chief of all the army commanders for the first month.
~4 Dodai (Dodo) the Ahohite (brother of rest) was in charge of the division for the second month, and Mikloth (staves) was the leader. There were 24,000 men in his division.
~5 The third army commander, as chief for the third month, was Benaiah (YHWH has built up) son of Jehoiada (YHWH knows) the priest. There were 24,000 men in his division.
~6 This Benaiah (YHWH has built up) was mighty among the Thirty and was over the Thirty, and his son Ammizabad (my people have bestowed) was in charge of his division.
~7 The fourth, for the fourth month, was Joab’s (YHWH is father) brother Asahel (God-made), and his son Zebadiah (endowment of YHWH) was commander after him. There were 24,000 men in his division.
~8 The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth (Shammah) the Izrahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
~9 The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira (watchful of a city) son of Ikkesh (twisted) the Tekoite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
~10 The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez (he has saved) the Pelonite (a certain one), an Ephraimite (doubly fruitful). There were 24,000 men in his division.
~11 The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai (weaver) the Hushathite, a Zerahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
~12 The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer (my father is help) the Anathothite, a Benjamite (son of the right hand). There were 24,000 men in his division.
~13 The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai (impetuous) the Netophathite, a Zerahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
~14 The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah (YHWH has built up) the Pirathonite, an Ephraimite (doubly fruitful). There were 24,000 men in his division.
~15 The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai (Heled) the Netophathite, from the family of Othniel (lion of God). There were 24,000 men in his division.
~16 These officers were in charge of the tribes of Israel (he wrestles with God): Over the Reubenites was Eliezer (God is my helper) son of Zichri (memorable); over the Simeonites was Shephatiah (YHWH has judged) son of Maacah (oppression);
~17 over Levi (joined to) was Hashabiah (YHWH has considered) son of Kemuel (raised of God); over Aaron (light bringer) was Zadok (righteous);
~18 over Judah (praised) was Elihu (He is my God), one of David’s (beloved) brothers; over Issachar (there is recompense) was Omri (pupil of YHWH) son of Michael (who is like God);
~19 over Zebulun (exalted) was Ishmaiah (YHWH will hear) son of Obadiah (servant of YHWH); over Naphtali (wrestling) was Jerimoth (He is Most High) son of Azriel (my help is God);
~20 over the Ephraimites (doubly fruitful) was Hoshea (salvation) son of Azaziah (YHWH is mighty); over one of the half-tribes of Manasseh (causing to forget) was Joel (YHWH is God) son of Pedaiah (YHWH has ransomed);
~21 over the half-tribe of Manasseh (causing to forget) in Gilead (rocky region) was Iddo (timely / lovely) son of Zechariah (YHWH remembers); over Benjamin (son of the right hand) was Jaasiel (God is maker) son of Abner (my father is a lamp);
~22 and over Dan (He has judged) was Azarel (God has helped) son of Jeroham (showing pity). These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel (he wrestles with God).
~23 David (beloved) did not count the men aged twenty or under, because the LORD {YHWH} had said that He would make Israel (he wrestles with God) as numerous as the stars of the sky.
~24 Joab (YHWH is father) son of Zeruiah (balsam) began to count the men but did not finish. For because of this census wrath came upon Israel (he wrestles with God), and the number was not entered in the Book of the Chronicles of King David (beloved).
~25 Azmaveth (strong unto death) son of Adiel (ornament of God) was in charge of the royal storehouses. Jonathan (YHWH has given) son of Uzziah (my strength is YHWH) was in charge of the storehouses in the country, in the cities, in the villages, and in the fortresses.
~26 Ezri (help of YHWH) son of Chelub (caged) was in charge of the workers in the fields who tilled the soil.
~27 Shimei (renowned) the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards. Zabdi (endowment) the Shiphmite was in charge of the produce of the vineyards for the wine vats.
~28 Baal-hanan (Baal is gracious) the Gederite (a wall) was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the foothills {Shephelah}. Joash (YHWH hastens) was in charge of the stores of olive oil.
~29 Shitrai (my officers) the Sharonite was in charge of the herds grazing in Sharon (a plain). Shaphat (He has judged) son of Adlai (justice of YHWH) was in charge of the herds in the valleys.
~30 Obil (camel driver) the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels. Jehdeiah (YHWH is unity) the Meronothite (joyful shouter) was in charge of the donkeys.
~31 Jaziz (He makes prominent) the Hagrite (wanderer) was in charge of the flocks. All these officials were in charge of King David’s (beloved) property.
~32 David’s (beloved) uncle Jonathan (YHWH has given) was a counselor; he was a man of insight and a scribe. Jehiel (God lives) son of Hachmoni (wise) attended to the sons of the king.
~33 Ahithophel (my brother is folly) was the king’s counselor. Hushai (hastening) the Archite (lengthy) was the king’s friend.
~34 Ahithophel (my brother is folly) was succeeded by Jehoiada (YHWH knows) son of Benaiah (YHWH has built up), then by Abiathar (my father is great). Joab (YHWH is father) was the commander of the king’s army.
chapters.1 Chronicles\u000028:
~1 Now David (beloved) summoned all the leaders of Israel (he wrestles with God) to Jerusalem (city of peace): the leaders of the tribes, the leaders of the divisions in the king’s service, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials in charge of all the property and cattle of the king and his sons, along with the court officials and mighty men—every mighty man of valor.
~2 Then King David (beloved) rose to his feet and said, “Listen to me, my brothers and my people. It was in my heart to build a house as a resting place for the ark of the covenant of the LORD {YHWH} and as a footstool for our God {Elohenu}. I had made preparations to build it,
~3 but God {Elohim} said to me, ‘You are not to build a house for My Name, because you are a man of war who has shed blood.’
~4 Yet the LORD, the God {YHWH Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God), chose me out of all my father’s house to be king over Israel forever. For He chose Judah (praised) as leader, and from the house of Judah He chose my father’s household, and from my father’s sons He was pleased to make me king over all Israel.
~5 And of all my sons—for the LORD {YHWH} has given me many sons—He has chosen Solomon (peace) my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel (he wrestles with God).
~6 And He said to me, ‘Solomon (peace) your son is the one who will build My house and My courts, for I have chosen him as My son, and I will be his Father.
~7 I will establish his kingdom forever, if he resolutely carries out My commandments and ordinances, as is being done this day.’
~8 So now in the sight of all Israel (he wrestles with God), the assembly of the LORD {YHWH}, and in the hearing of our God {Elohenu}, keep and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your⁺ God, so that you⁺ may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your⁺ descendants forever.
~9 As for you, Solomon (peace) my son, know the God {Elohe} of your father and serve Him wholeheartedly and with a willing mind, for the LORD {YHWH} searches every heart and understands the intent of every thought. If you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will reject you forever.
~10 Consider now that the LORD {YHWH} has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it.”
~11 Then David (beloved) gave his son Solomon (peace) the plans for the portico of the temple, its buildings, storehouses, upper rooms, inner rooms, and the room for the mercy seat (atonement cover).
~12 The plans contained everything David had in mind {ruach} for the courts of the house of the LORD {YHWH}, for all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of the house of God {Elohim} and of the dedicated things,
~13 for the divisions of the priests and Levites, for all the work of service in the house of the LORD {YHWH}, and for all the articles of service in the house of the LORD:
~14 the weight of all the gold articles for every kind of service; the weight of all the silver articles for every kind of service;
~15 the weight of the gold lampstands and their lamps, including the weight of each lampstand and its lamps; the weight of each silver lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;
~16 the weight of gold for each table of showbread, and of silver for the silver tables;
~17 the weight of the pure gold for the forks, sprinkling bowls, and pitchers; the weight of each gold dish; the weight of each silver bowl;
~18 the weight of the refined gold for the altar of incense; and the plans for the chariot of the gold cherubim that spread their wings and overshadowed the ark of the covenant of the LORD {YHWH}.
~19 “All this,” said David, “all the details of this plan, the LORD {YHWH} has made clear to me in writing by His hand upon me.”
~20 David also (beloved) said to Solomon (peace) his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God {YHWH Elohim}, my God, is with you. He will neither fail you nor forsake you before all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.
~21 The divisions of the priests and Levites are ready for all the service of the house of God {Elohim}, and every willing man of every skill will be at your disposal for the work. The officials and all the people are fully at your command.”
chapters.1 Chronicles\u000029:
~1 Then King David (beloved) said to the whole assembly, “My son Solomon (peace), the one whom God {Elohim} has chosen, is young and inexperienced. The task is great because this palace is not for man, but for the LORD {YHWH} God.
~2 Now with all my ability I have made provision for the house of my God {Elohay}—gold for the gold articles, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron, and wood for the wood, as well as onyx for the settings, turquoise, stones of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and slabs of marble—all in abundance.
~3 Moreover, because of my delight in the house of my God {Elohay}, I now give for it my personal treasures of gold and silver, over and above all that I have provided for this holy temple:
~4 three thousand talents of gold <113 t / 103 mt> (the gold of Ophir (reducing to ashes)) and seven thousand talents of refined silver <264 t / 239.5 mt>, to overlay the walls of the buildings,
~5 for the gold work and the silver work, and for all the work to be done by the craftsmen. Now who is willing to consecrate himself to the LORD {YHWH} today?”
~6 Then the leaders of the families, the officers of the tribes of Israel (he wrestles with God), the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king’s work gave willingly.
~7 Toward the service of God’s house they gave 5,000 talents <188.5 t / 171 mt> and 10,000 darics of gold <185.2 lb / 84 kg>, 10,000 talents of silver <377 t / 342 mt>, 18,000 talents of bronze <678.6 t / 615.6 mt>, and 100,000 talents of iron <3,770 t / 3,420 mt>.
~8 Whoever had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD {YHWH}, under the care of Jehiel (Jehieli) the Gershonite.
~9 And the people rejoiced at the willing response of their leaders, for they had given to the LORD freely {YHWH} and wholeheartedly. And King David (beloved) also rejoiced greatly.
~10 Then David (beloved) blessed the LORD {YHWH} in the sight of all the assembly and said: “May You be blessed, O LORD, God {YHWH Elohe} of our father Israel (he wrestles with God), from everlasting to everlasting.
~11 Yours, O LORD {YHWH}, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the splendor and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth belongs to You. Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom, and You are exalted as head over all.
~12 Both riches and honor come from You, and You are the ruler over all. In Your hands are power and might to exalt and give strength to all.
~13 Now therefore, our God {Elohenu}, we give You thanks, and we praise Your glorious name.
~14 But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? For everything comes from You, and from Your own hand we have given to You.
~15 For we are foreigners and strangers in Your presence, as were all our forefathers. Our days on earth are like a shadow, without hope.
~16 O LORD our God {YHWH Elohenu}, from Your hand comes all this abundance that we have provided to build You a house for Your holy Name, and all of it belongs to You.
~17 I know, my God {Elohay}, that You test the heart and delight in uprightness. All these things I have given willingly and with an upright heart, and now I have seen Your people who are present here giving joyfully and willingly to You.
~18 O LORD, God {YHWH Elohe} of our fathers Abraham (father of many), Isaac (he laughs), and Israel (he wrestles with God), keep this desire forever in the intentions of the hearts of Your people, and direct their hearts toward You.
~19 And give my son Solomon (peace) a whole heart to keep and carry out all Your commandments, decrees, and statutes, and to build Your palace for which I have made provision.”
~20 Then David (beloved) said to the whole assembly, “Bless the LORD your⁺ God {YHWH Eloheikem}.” So the whole assembly blessed the LORD, the God of their fathers. They bowed down and paid homage to the LORD and to the king.
~21 The next day they offered sacrifices {YHWH} and presented burnt offerings to the LORD: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, along with their drink offerings, and other sacrifices in abundance for all Israel (he wrestles with God).
~22 That day they ate and drank with great joy in the presence of the LORD {YHWH}. Then, for a second time, they designated David’s (beloved) son Solomon (peace) as king, anointing him before the LORD as ruler, and Zadok (righteous) as the priest.
~23 So Solomon (peace) sat on the throne of the LORD {YHWH} as king in place of his father David (beloved). He prospered, and all Israel (he wrestles with God) obeyed him.
~24 All the officials and mighty men, as well as all of King David’s (beloved) sons, pledged their allegiance to King Solomon (peace).
~25 The LORD {YHWH} highly exalted Solomon (peace) in the sight of all Israel (he wrestles with God) and bestowed on him royal majesty such as had not been bestowed on any king in Israel before him.
~26 David (beloved) son of Jesse (I possess) was king over all Israel (he wrestles with God).
~27 The length of David’s reign over Israel (he wrestles with God) was forty years—seven years in Hebron (association) and thirty-three years in Jerusalem (city of peace).
~28 He died at a ripe old age, full of years, riches, and honor, and his son Solomon (peace) reigned in his place.
~29 Now the acts of King David (beloved), from first to last, are indeed written in the Chronicles of Samuel (his name is El) the Seer, the Chronicles of Nathan (giver) the Prophet, and the Chronicles of Gad (troop) the Seer,
~30 together with all the details of his reign, his might, and the circumstances that came upon him and Israel (he wrestles with God) and all the kingdoms of the lands.
chapters.2 Chronicles\u00001:
~1 Now Solomon (peace) son of David (beloved) established himself securely over his kingdom, and the LORD his God {YHWH Elohaw} was with him and highly exalted him.
~2 Then Solomon (peace) spoke to all Israel (he wrestles with God), to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel—the heads of the families.
~3 And Solomon (peace) and the whole assembly went to the high place at Gibeon (hill city) because it was the location of God’s Tent of Meeting, which Moses (drawn out) the servant of the LORD {YHWH} had made in the wilderness.
~4 Now David (beloved) (city of forests) had brought the ark of God {Elohim} from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, because he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem (city of peace).
~5 But the bronze altar made by Bezalel (in the shadow of God) son of Uri (fiery), the son of Hur (hole), was in Gibeon before [was there before; MT he placed before] the tabernacle of the LORD {YHWH}. So Solomon (peace) and the assembly inquired of Him there.
~6 Solomon (peace) offered sacrifices there before the LORD {YHWH} on the bronze altar at the Tent of Meeting, where he offered a thousand burnt offerings.
~7 That night God {Elohim} appeared to Solomon (peace) and said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”
~8 Solomon (peace) replied to God {Elohim}: “You have shown much loving devotion {chesed} to my father David (beloved), and You have made me king in his place.
~9 Now, O LORD God {YHWH Elohim}, let Your promise to my father David (beloved) be fulfilled. For You have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
~10 Now grant me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may lead this people \so that I may go out before this people and come in/. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”
~11 God {Elohim} said to Solomon (peace), “Since this was in your heart instead of requesting riches or wealth or honor for yourself or death for your enemies—and since you have not even requested long life but have asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern My people over whom I have made you king—
~12 therefore wisdom and knowledge have been granted to you. And I will also give you riches and wealth and honor unlike anything given to the kings before you or after you.”
~13 So Solomon (peace) went to Jerusalem (city of peace) from the high place in Gibeon (hill city), from before the Tent of Meeting, and he reigned over Israel (he wrestles with God).
~14 Solomon (peace) accumulated \Solomon accumulated chariots and horses; he had/ 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses (horsemen), which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem (city of peace).
~15 The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem (city of peace) as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills {Shephelah}.
~16 Solomon’s (peace) horses were imported from Egypt (land of bondage) and Kue (Cilicia); the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.
~17 A chariot could be imported from Egypt (land of bondage) for six hundred shekels of silver <15.1 lb / 6.8 kg>, and a horse for a hundred and fifty <3.8 lb / 1.7 kg>. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram (exalted).
chapters.2 Chronicles\u00002:
~1 Now Solomon (peace) purposed to build a house for the Name of the LORD {YHWH} and a royal palace for himself.
~2 So he conscripted (peace) 70,000 porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors.
~3 Then Solomon (peace) sent word to Hiram \Huram/ king of Tyre (a rock): “Do for me as you did for my father David (beloved) when you sent him cedars to build himself a house to live in.
~4 Behold, I am about to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God {YHWH Elohay} to dedicate to Him for burning fragrant incense before Him, for displaying the showbread continuously, and for making burnt offerings every morning and evening as well as on the Sabbaths, New Moons, and appointed feasts of the LORD our God. This is ordained for Israel forever (he wrestles with God).
~5 The house that I am building will be great, for our God {Elohenu} is greater than all gods.
~6 But who is able to build a house for Him, since the heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain Him? Who then am I, that I should build a house for Him, except as a place to burn sacrifices before Him?
~7 Send me, therefore, a craftsman skilled in engraving to work with gold and silver, with bronze and iron, and with purple, crimson, and blue yarn. He will work with my craftsmen in Judah (praised) and Jerusalem (city of peace), whom my father David (beloved) provided.
~8 Send me also cedar, cypress (pine), and algum (almug) logs from Lebanon (whiteness), for I know that your servants have skill to cut timber there. And indeed, my servants will work with yours
~9 to prepare for me timber in abundance, because the temple I am building will be great and wonderful.
~10 I will pay your servants, the woodcutters, 20,000 cors of ground wheat <124,800 bu / 4.4M l>, 20,000 cors of barley, 20,000 baths of wine <116,000 gal / 440,000 l>, and 20,000 baths of olive oil.
~11 Then Hiram (noble born) king of Tyre (a rock) wrote a letter in reply to Solomon (peace): “Because the LORD {YHWH} loves His people, He has set you over them as king.”
~12 And Hiram (noble born) added: “Blessed be the LORD, the God {YHWH Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God), who made the heavens and the earth! He has given King David (beloved) a wise son with insight and understanding, who will build a temple for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
~13 So now I am sending you Huram-abi (noble born), a skillful man endowed with creativity (understanding).
~14 He is the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan (He has judged), and his father is a man of Tyre. He is skilled in work with gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, purple, blue, and crimson yarn, and fine linen. He is experienced in every kind of engraving and can execute any design that is given him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my lord, your father David (beloved).
~15 Now let my lord send to his servants the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine he promised.
~16 We will cut logs from Lebanon (whiteness), as many as you need, and we will float them to you as rafts by sea down to Joppa (beautiful). Then you can take them up to Jerusalem (city of peace).”
~17 Solomon (peace) numbered all the foreign men in the land of Israel (he wrestles with God) following the census his father David had conducted (beloved), and there were found to be 153,600 in all.
~18 Solomon made 70,000 of them porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors.
chapters.2 Chronicles\u00003:
~1 Then Solomon (peace) began to build the house of the LORD {YHWH} in Jerusalem (city of peace) on Mount Moriah (chosen by YHWH), where the LORD had appeared [where He had appeared] to his father David (beloved). This was the place that David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan (Araunah) the Jebusite (Jerusalemite).
~2 Solomon began construction on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.
~3 The foundation that Solomon (peace) laid for the house of God {Elohim} was sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide <90 ft x 30 ft / 27.4 m x 9.1 m>, according to the old standard.
~4 The portico at the front, extending across the width of the temple, was twenty cubits long <30 ft / 9.1 m> and twenty cubits high <180 ft / 54.9 m>. He overlaid the inside with pure gold.
~5 He paneled the main room with cypress (pine), which he overlaid with fine gold and decorated with palm trees and chains.
~6 He adorned the temple with precious stones for beauty, and its gold was from Parvaim (oriental regions).
~7 He overlaid its beams, thresholds, walls, and doors with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
~8 Then he made the Most Holy Place (the Holy of Holies); its length corresponded to the width of the temple—twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. And he overlaid the inside with six hundred talents of fine gold <22.6 t / 20.5 mt>.
~9 The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold <1.26 lb / 569.8 g>. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
~10 In the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work, and he overlaid them with gold.
~11 The total wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long <7.5 ft / 2.3 m> and touched the wall of the temple, and its other wing was five cubits long and touched the wing of the other cherub.
~12 The wing of the second cherub also measured five cubits and touched the wall of the temple, while its other wing measured five cubits and touched the wing of the first cherub.
~13 So the total wingspan of these cherubim was twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing the main room.
~14 He made the veil of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim woven into it.
~15 In front of the temple he made two pillars, which together were thirty-five cubits high <52.5 ft / 16 m>, each with a capital on top measuring five cubits.
~16 He made interwoven chains (He made chains in the inner sanctuary) and put them on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them into the chainwork.
~17 Then he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the south and one on the north. The pillar on the south he named Jachin (He establishes), and the pillar on the north he named Boaz (in Him is strength).
chapters.2 Chronicles\u00005:
~1 So all the work that Solomon (peace) had performed for the house of the LORD {YHWH} was completed. Then Solomon brought in the items his father David (beloved) had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and all the furnishings—and he placed them in the treasuries of the house of God {Elohim}.
~2 At that time Solomon (peace) assembled in Jerusalem (city of peace) the elders of Israel (he wrestles with God)—all the tribal heads and family leaders of the Israelites—to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD {YHWH} from Zion, the City of David (beloved).
~3 So all the men of Israel (he wrestles with God) came together to the king at the feast in the seventh month (the Feast of Tabernacles).
~4 When all the elders of Israel (he wrestles with God) had arrived, the Levites took up the ark,
~5 and they brought up the ark and the Tent of Meeting with all its sacred furnishings. The Levitical priests carried them up.
~6 There, before the ark, King Solomon (peace) and the whole congregation of Israel (he wrestles with God) who had assembled with him sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
~7 Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD {YHWH} to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place (the Holy of Holies), beneath the wings of the cherubim.
~8 For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadowed the ark and its poles.
~9 The poles of the ark extended far enough that their ends were visible from in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place \not from outside/; and they are there to this day.
~10 There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses (drawn out) had placed in it at Horeb (Mount Sinai), where the LORD {YHWH} had made a covenant with the Israelites (God prevails) after they had come out of Egypt (land of bondage).
~11 Now all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves regardless of their divisions. And when the priests came out of the Holy Place,
~12 all the Levitical singers—Asaph (gatherer), Heman (faithful), Jeduthun (praising), and their sons and relatives—stood on the east side of the altar, dressed in fine linen and playing cymbals, harps, and lyres, accompanied by 120 priests sounding trumpets.
~13 The trumpeters and singers joined together to praise and thank the LORD {YHWH} with one voice. They lifted up their voices, accompanied by trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments, in praise to the LORD: “For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.” And the temple, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud
~14 so that the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud. For the glory of the LORD {YHWH} filled the house of God {Elohim}.
chapters.2 Chronicles\u00006:
~1 Then Solomon (peace) declared: “The LORD {YHWH} has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud.
~2 But I have built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.”
~3 And as the whole assembly of Israel (he wrestles with God) stood there, the king turned around and blessed them all
~4 and said: “Blessed be the LORD, the God {YHWH Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God), who has fulfilled with His own hand what He spoke with His mouth to my father David (beloved), saying,
~5 ‘Since the day I brought My people out of the land of Egypt (land of bondage), I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel (he wrestles with God) in which to build a house so that My Name would be there, nor have I chosen anyone to be ruler over My people Israel.
~6 But now I have chosen Jerusalem (city of peace) for My Name to be there, and I have chosen David (beloved) to be over My people Israel (he wrestles with God).’
~7 Now it was in the heart of my father David (beloved) to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God {YHWH Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God).
~8 But the LORD {YHWH} said to my father David (beloved), ‘Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well to have this in your heart.
~9 Nevertheless, you are not the one to build it; but your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name.’
~10 Now the LORD {YHWH} has fulfilled the word that He spoke. I have succeeded my father David (beloved), and I sit on the throne of Israel (he wrestles with God), as the LORD promised. I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God {Elohe} of Israel.
~11 And there I have placed the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD {YHWH} that He made with the children of Israel (he wrestles with God).”
~12 Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD {YHWH} in front of the whole assembly of Israel (he wrestles with God) and spread out his hands.
~13 Now Solomon (peace) had made a bronze platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high <7.5 ft x 7.5 ft x 4.5 ft / 2.3 m x 2.3 m x 1.4 m> and had placed it in the middle of the courtyard. He stood on it, knelt down before the whole assembly of Israel (he wrestles with God), spread out his hands toward heaven,
~14 and said: “O LORD, God {YHWH Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God), there is no God like You in heaven or on earth, keeping Your covenant of loving devotion with Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts.
~15 You have kept Your promise to Your servant, my father David (beloved). What You spoke with Your mouth You have fulfilled with Your hand this day.
~16 Therefore now, O LORD, God {YHWH Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God), keep for Your servant, my father David (beloved), what You promised when You said: ‘You will never fail to have a man to sit before Me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants guard their way to walk in My law as you have walked before Me.’
~17 And now, O LORD, God {YHWH Elohe} of Israel (he wrestles with God), please confirm what You promised to Your servant David (beloved).
~18 But will God {Elohim} indeed dwell with man upon the earth? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.
~19 Yet regard the prayer and plea of Your servant, O LORD my God {YHWH Elohay}, so that You may hear the cry and the prayer that Your servant is praying before You.
~20 May Your eyes be open toward this temple day and night, toward the place where You said You would put Your Name, so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
~21 Hear the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel (he wrestles with God) when they pray toward this place. May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place. May You hear and forgive.
~22 When a man sins against his neighbor and is required to take an oath, and he comes to take an oath before Your altar in this temple,
~23 then may You hear from heaven and act. May You judge Your servants, condemning the wicked man by bringing down on his own head what he has done, and justifying the righteous man by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
~24 When Your people Israel (he wrestles with God) are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You and confess Your name, praying and pleading before You in this temple,
~25 then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel (he wrestles with God). May You restore them to the land You gave to them and their fathers.
~26 When the skies are shut and there is no rain because Your people have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and they turn from their sins because You have afflicted them,
~27 then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel (he wrestles with God), so that You may teach them the good way in which they should walk. May You send rain on the land that You gave Your people as an inheritance.
~28 When famine or plague comes upon the land, or blight or mildew or locusts or grasshoppers, or when their enemies besiege them in their cities, whatever plague or sickness may come,
~29 then may whatever prayer or plea Your people Israel (he wrestles with God) make—each knowing his own afflictions and spreading out his hands toward this temple—
~30 be heard by You from heaven, Your dwelling place. And may You forgive and repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart—for You alone know the hearts of men—
~31 so that they may fear You and walk in Your ways all the days they live in the land that You gave to our fathers.
~32 And as for the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel (he wrestles with God) but has come from a distant land because of Your great name and Your mighty hand and outstretched arm—when he comes and prays toward this temple,
~33 then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to You. Then all the peoples of the earth will know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel (he wrestles with God), and they will know that this house I have built is called by Your Name.
~34 When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and when they pray to You in the direction of this city You have chosen and the house I have built for Your Name,
~35 then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.
~36 When they sin against You—for there is no one who does not sin—and You become angry with them and deliver them to an enemy who takes them as captives to a land far or near,
~37 and when they come to their senses in the land to which they were taken, and they repent and plead with You in the land of their captors, saying, ‘We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly,’
~38 and when they return to You with all their heart and soul in the land of the enemies who took them captive, and when they pray in the direction of the land that You gave to their fathers, the city You have chosen, and the house I have built for Your Name,
~39 then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, their prayer and pleas, and may You uphold their cause. May You forgive Your people who sinned against You.
~40 Now, my God {Elohay}, may Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place.
~41 Now therefore, arise, O LORD God {YHWH Elohim}, and enter Your resting place, You and the ark of Your might. May Your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and may Your godly ones rejoice in goodness.
~42 O LORD God {YHWH Elohim}, do not reject Your anointed one. Remember Your loving devotion to Your servant David (beloved).”
chapters.2 Chronicles\u00007:
~1 When Solomon (peace) had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD {YHWH} filled the temple.
~2 The priests were unable to enter the house of the LORD {YHWH}, because the glory of the LORD had filled it.
~3 When all the Israelites (God prevails) saw the fire coming down and the glory of the LORD {YHWH} above the temple, they bowed down on the pavement with their faces to the ground, and they worshiped and gave thanks to the LORD: “For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.”
~4 Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD {YHWH}.
~5 And King Solomon (peace) offered a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God {Elohim}.
~6 The priests stood at their posts, as did the Levites with the musical instruments of the LORD {YHWH}, which King David (beloved) had made for giving thanks to the LORD and with which David had offered praise, saying, “For His loving devotion endures forever.” Across from the Levites, the priests sounded trumpets, and all the Israelites (God prevails) were standing.
~7 Then Solomon (peace) consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD {YHWH}, and there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, since the bronze altar he had made could not hold all these offerings.
~8 So at that time Solomon (peace) and all Israel (he wrestles with God) with him—a very great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath (fortress) to the Brook of Egypt (land of bondage)—kept the feast (the Feast of Tabernacles) for seven days.
~9 On the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for the dedication of the altar had lasted seven days, and the feast seven days more.
~10 On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent the people away to their homes, joyful and glad of heart for the good things that the LORD {YHWH} had done for David (beloved), for Solomon (peace), and for His people Israel (he wrestles with God).
~11 When Solomon (peace) had finished the house of the LORD {YHWH} and the royal palace, successfully carrying out all that was in his heart to do for the house of the LORD and for his own palace,
~12 the LORD {YHWH} appeared to him (peace) at night and said to him: “I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.
~13 If I close the sky so there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send a plague among My people,
~14 and if My people who are called by My name humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
~15 Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.
~16 For I have now chosen and consecrated this temple so that My Name may be there forever. My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.
~17 And as for you, if you walk before Me as your father David (beloved) walked, doing all I have commanded you, and if you keep My statutes and ordinances,
~18 then I will establish your royal throne, as I covenanted with your father David (beloved) when I said, ‘You will never fail to have a man to rule over Israel (he wrestles with God).’
~19 But if you⁺ turn away and forsake the statutes and commandments I have set before you⁺, and if you⁺ go off to serve and worship other gods,
~20 then I will uproot Israel from the soil I have given them, and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name. I will make it an object of scorn and ridicule among all the peoples.
~21 And when this temple has become a heap of rubble [And though this temple is now exalted], all who pass by it will be appalled and say, ‘Why has the LORD {YHWH} done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’
~22 And others will answer, ‘Because they have forsaken the LORD, the God {YHWH Elohe} of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt (land of bondage), and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them—because of this, He has brought all this disaster upon them.’”
chapters.2 Chronicles\u00008:
~1 Now at the end of the twenty years during which Solomon (peace) had built the house of the LORD {YHWH} and his own palace,
~2 Solomon (peace) rebuilt the cities Hiram \Huram/ had given him and settled Israelites (God prevails) there.
~3 Then Solomon (peace) went to Hamath-zobah (fortress of Zobah) and captured it.
~4 He built Tadmor (palm tree) in the wilderness, in addition to all the store cities that he had built in Hamath (fortress).
~5 He rebuilt (house of hollowness) Upper and Lower Beth-horon as fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars,
~6 as well as Baalath (mistress), all the store cities that belonged to Solomon (peace), and all the cities for his chariots and horses (horsemen) whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem (city of peace), Lebanon (whiteness), and throughout the land of his dominion.
~7 As for all the people who remained of the Hittites, Amorites (sayers), Perizzites (villagers), Hivites, and Jebusites (Jerusalemites) (these people were not Israelites (God prevails))—
~8 their descendants who remained in the land, those whom the Israelites (God prevails) had not destroyed—Solomon (peace) conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day.
~9 But Solomon (peace) did not consign any of the Israelites (God prevails) to slave labor, because they were his men of war, the leaders of his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
~10 They were also the chief officers for King Solomon (peace): 250 supervisors.
~11 Solomon (peace) brought the daughter of Pharaoh (great house) up from the City of David (beloved) to the palace he had built for her. For he said, “My wife must not live in the house of David king of Israel (he wrestles with God), because the places the ark of the LORD {YHWH} has entered are holy.”
~12 At that time Solomon (peace) offered burnt offerings to the LORD {YHWH} on the altar of the LORD he had built in front of the portico.
~13 He observed the daily requirement for offerings according to the commandment of Moses (drawn out) for Sabbaths, New Moons, and the three annual appointed feasts—the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot), and the Feast of Tabernacles (Sukkot).
~14 In keeping with the ordinances of his father David (beloved), Solomon appointed the divisions of the priests over their service, and the Levites for their duties to offer praise and to minister before the priests according to the daily requirement. He also appointed gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate, for this had been the command of David, the man of God {Elohim}.
~15 They did not turn aside from the king’s command regarding the priests or the Levites in any matter, including that of the treasuries.
~16 Thus all the work of Solomon (peace) was carried out, from the day the foundation was laid for the house of the LORD {YHWH} until it was finished. So the house of the LORD was completed.
~17 Then Solomon (peace) went to Ezion-geber (backbone) and to Eloth (Elath) on the coast of Edom.
~18 So Hiram (noble born) sent him ships captained by his servants, along with crews of experienced sailors. They went with Solomon’s (peace) servants to Ophir (reducing to ashes) and acquired from there 450 talents of gold <17 t / 15.4 mt>, which they delivered to King Solomon.
chapters.2 Chronicles\u00009:
~1 Now when the queen of Sheba (seven) heard about the fame of Solomon (peace), she came to test him with difficult questions. She arrived in Jerusalem (city of peace) with a very large caravan—with camels bearing spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones. And she came to Solomon and spoke with him about all that was on her mind.
~2 And Solomon (peace) answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for him to explain.
~3 When the queen of Sheba (seven) saw the wisdom of Solomon (peace), the palace he had built,
~4 the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the service and attire of his attendants, the attire of his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented [and his stairway by which he went up] at the house of the LORD {YHWH}, it took her breath away {ruach}.
~5 She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your words (your achievements) and wisdom is true.
~6 But I did not believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not half of the greatness of your wisdom was told to me. You have far exceeded the report I heard.
~7 How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
~8 Blessed be the LORD your God {YHWH Eloheka}, who has delighted in you to set you on His throne to be king for the LORD your God. Because your God loved Israel (he wrestles with God) enough to establish them forever, He has made you king over them to carry out justice and righteousness.”
~9 Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold <4.52 t / 4.1 mt>, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. There had never been such spices as those the queen of Sheba (seven) gave to King Solomon (peace).
~10 (The servants of Hiram (noble) and of Solomon (peace) who brought gold from Ophir (reducing to ashes) also brought algum (almug) wood and precious stones.
~11 The king made the algum wood into steps (gateways) for the house of the LORD {YHWH} and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Never before had anything like them been seen in the land of Judah (praised).)
~12 King Solomon (peace) gave the queen of Sheba (seven) all she desired—whatever she asked—far more than she had brought the king. Then she left and returned to her own country, along with her servants.
~13 The weight of gold that came to Solomon (peace) each year was 666 talents <25.1 t / 22.8 mt>,
~14 not including the revenue from the merchants and traders. And all the Arabian kings and governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon (peace).
~15 King Solomon (peace) made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of hammered gold <15.1 lb / 6.8 kg> went into each shield.
~16 He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three hundred shekels of gold <7.5 lb / 3.4 kg> went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon (whiteness).
~17 Additionally, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
~18 The throne had six steps, and a footstool of gold was attached to it. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.
~19 Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like this had ever been made for any kingdom.
~20 All King Solomon’s (peace) drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon (whiteness) were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.
~21 For the king had the ships of Tarshish (a fleet of trading ships) that went with Hiram’s \Huram’s/ servants, and once every three years the ships of Tarshish (yellow jasper) would arrive bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks (baboons).
~22 So King Solomon (peace) surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
~23 All the kings of the earth sought an audience with Solomon (peace) to hear the wisdom that God {Elohim} had put in his heart.
~24 Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
~25 Solomon (peace) had 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots, and 12,000 horses (horsemen), which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem (city of peace).
~26 He reigned over all the kings from the Euphrates \the River/ to the land of the Philistines (immigrants), as far as the border of Egypt (land of bondage).
~27 The king made silver as common in Jerusalem (city of peace) as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills {Shephelah}.
~28 Solomon’s (peace) horses were imported from Egypt (land of bondage) and from all the lands.
~29 As for the rest of the acts of Solomon (peace), from beginning to end, are they not written in the Records of Nathan (giver) the Prophet, in the Prophecy of Ahijah (brother of Yah) the Shilonite, and in the Visions of Iddo (appointed) the Seer concerning Jeroboam (the people will contend) son of Nebat (aspect)?
~30 Solomon (peace) reigned in Jerusalem (city of peace) over all Israel (he wrestles with God) forty years.
~31 And Solomon (peace) rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David (beloved). And his son Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) reigned in his place.
chapters.2 Chronicles\u000010:
~1 Then Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) went to Shechem (shoulder), for all Israel (he wrestles with God) had gone there to make him king.
~2 When Jeroboam (the people will contend) son of Nebat (aspect) heard about this, he returned from Egypt (land of bondage), where he had fled from King Solomon (peace).
~3 So they sent for Jeroboam, and he (the people will contend) and all Israel (he wrestles with God) came to Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) and said,
~4 “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you must lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
~5 Rehoboam answered, “Come back to me in three days.” So the people departed.
~6 Then King Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon (peace) during his lifetime. “How do you⁺ advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.
~7 They replied, “If you will be kind to these people and please them by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
~8 But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
~9 He asked them, “What message do you⁺ advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
~10 The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
~11 Whereas my father burdened you⁺ with a heavy yoke, I will add to your⁺ yoke. Whereas my father scourged you⁺ with whips, I will scourge you⁺ with scorpions.’”
~12 After three days, Jeroboam (the people will contend) and all the people returned to Rehoboam (a people has enlarged), since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
~13 And the king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) rejected the advice of the elders
~14 and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your⁺ yoke heavy [Whereas I made your yoke heavy], I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you⁺ with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”
~15 So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from God {Elohim}, in order that the LORD {YHWH} might fulfill the word that He had spoken through Ahijah (brother of Yah) the Shilonite to Jeroboam (the people will contend) son of Nebat (aspect).
~16 When all Israel saw (he wrestles with God) that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David (beloved), and what inheritance in the son of Jesse (I possess)? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” So all the Israelites went home,
~17 but Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) still reigned over the Israelites (God prevails) living in the cities of Judah (praised).
~18 Then King Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) sent out Hadoram (Adoniram), who was in charge of the forced labor, but the Israelites (God prevails) stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem (city of peace).
~19 So to this day Israel (he wrestles with God) has been in rebellion against the house of David (beloved).
chapters.2 Chronicles\u000011:
~1 When Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) arrived in Jerusalem (city of peace), he mobilized the house of Judah (praised) and Benjamin (son of the right hand)—180,000 chosen warriors—to fight against Israel (he wrestles with God) and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
~2 But the word of the LORD {YHWH} came to Shemaiah (heard by YHWH) the man of God {Elohim}:
~3 “Tell Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) son of Solomon (peace) king of Judah (praised) and all the Israelites (God prevails) in Judah and Benjamin (son of the right hand)
~4 that this is what the LORD {YHWH} says: ‘You⁺ are not to go up and fight against your⁺ brothers. Each of you⁺ must return home, for this is My doing.’” So they listened to the words of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam (the people will contend).
~5 Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) lived in Jerusalem (city of peace), and he built up cities for defense in Judah (praised).
~6 He built up Bethlehem (house of bread), Etam (lair of wild beasts), Tekoa (a stockade),
~7 Beth-zur (house of the rock), Soco (bushy), Adullam (justice of the people),
~8 Gath (winepress), Mareshah (crest of a hill), Ziph (battlement),
~9 Adoraim (double glory), Lachish (invincible), Azekah (dug over),
~10 Zorah (hornet), Aijalon (field of deer), and Hebron (association), the fortified cities in Judah (praised) and Benjamin (son of the right hand).
~11 He strengthened their fortifications and put officers in them, with supplies of food, oil, and wine.
~12 He also put shields and spears in all the cities and strengthened them greatly. So Judah (praised) and Benjamin (son of the right hand) belonged to him.
~13 Moreover, the priests and Levites from all their districts throughout Israel (he wrestles with God) stood with Rehoboam.
~14 For the Levites left their pasturelands and their possessions and went to Judah (praised) and Jerusalem (city of peace), because Jeroboam (the people will contend) and his sons had rejected them as priests of the LORD {YHWH}.
~15 And Jeroboam appointed his own priests for the high places and for the goat demons and calf idols he had made.
~16 Those from every tribe of Israel (he wrestles with God) who had set their hearts to seek the LORD {YHWH} their God {Elohe} followed the Levites to Jerusalem (city of peace) to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
~17 So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah (praised) and supported Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) son of Solomon (peace) for three years, because they walked for three years in the way of David (beloved) and Solomon.
~18 And Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) married Mahalath (weak), who was the daughter of David’s (beloved) son Jerimoth (He is Most High) and of Abihail (my father is might), the daughter of Jesse’s (I possess) son Eliab (God is father).
~19 She bore sons to him: Jeush (He hurries to aid), Shemariah (kept by YHWH), and Zaham (loathing).
~20 After her, he married Maacah (oppression) daughter of Absalom (my father is peace), and she bore to him Abijah (YHWH is my father), Attai (opportune), Ziza (shining), and Shelomith (peaceful).
~21 Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) loved Maacah (oppression) daughter of Absalom (my father is peace) more than all his wives and concubines. In all, he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he was the father of twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
~22 Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) appointed Abijah (YHWH is my father) son of Maacah (oppression) as chief prince among his brothers, intending to make him king.
~23 Rehoboam also acted wisely by dispersing some of his sons throughout the districts of Judah (praised) and Benjamin (son of the right hand), and to all the fortified cities. He gave them abundant provisions and sought many wives for them.
chapters.2 Chronicles\u000012:
~1 After Rehoboam had established his (a people has enlarged) sovereignty and royal power, he and all Israel (Judah) with him forsook the Law of the LORD {YHWH}.
~2 In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s (a people has enlarged) reign, because they had been unfaithful to the LORD {YHWH}, Shishak (greedy of fine linen) king of Egypt (land of bondage) attacked Jerusalem (city of peace)
~3 with 1,200 chariots, 60,000 horsemen (charioteers), and countless troops who came with him out of Egypt (land of bondage)—Libyans (empty-hearted Da 11:43 / afflicted Jer 46:9), Sukkites (booth dwellers), and Cushites (people from the upper Nile region).
~4 He captured the fortified cities of Judah (praised) and came as far as Jerusalem (city of peace).
~5 Then Shemaiah (heard by YHWH) the prophet came to Rehoboam (a people has enlarged) and the leaders of Judah (praised) who had gathered at Jerusalem (city of peace) because of Shishak (greedy of fine linen), and he said to them, “This is what the LORD {YHWH} says: ‘You⁺ have forsaken Me; therefore, I have forsaken you⁺ into the hand of Shishak.’”
~6 So the leaders of Israel (he wrestles with God) and the king humbled themselves and said, “The LORD is {YHWH} righteous.”
~7 When the LORD {YHWH} saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah (heard by YHWH), saying, “They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them, but will soon grant them deliverance. My wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem (city of peace) through Shishak (greedy of fine linen).
~8 Nevertheless, they will become his servants, so that they may learn the difference between serving Me and serving the kings of other lands.”
